I replied to this but it was lost due to Voat over capacity. I'm going to keep this brief (and copy before hitting submit):

1) Bugs in your gut probably took thousands to millions of years to evolve into symbiotic organisms. Countless people probably died of infections as this relationship developed.

2) Even if you could engineer lactic-acid-loving bugs (like those described in the article) to survive inside people, designing them to not then try to invade their host completely would be much more difficult.

3a) The bugs in your gut live mostly off of excess nutrients you can't process / absorb

3b) They don't make beneficial things like antibiotics for you, to our knowledge ...which leads us to...

3c) Even if you could engineer symbiotic bugs that could somehow live safely within people, getting them to keep producing beneficial compounds in their new environment (your body) would probably be ~impossible. The microbes produce those compounds because they're beneficial in their current, lactic-acid-rich environment. By drastically changing their environment, you drastically change the pathogens they have in their environment. So, the microbes will stop producing the same compounds to defend themselves, probably over a period of days to weeks. We observe this in the lab; microbial resistance to antibiotics is not permanent for entire populations.

The entire premise is deceptive, as best I can tell. They want money to start a line of health foods that's based only loosely on any kind of science.

In brief -- there's a reason doctors have you taking penicillin pills and not eating plates of Penicillium notatum, and it's not because they didn't think of that first.
